weeks.headline: Before you automate it, follow one real case.
weeks.supporting_line: The exceptions hide in the handoffs—not in the happy-path flowchart.
weeks.companion_post: Tell a short story about shadowing a real workflow before deciding what to automate. Show the steps and the surprise.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: The exceptions hide in the handoffs—not in the happy-path flowchart.

weeks.headline: A sent email is an activity. A useful reply is progress.
weeks.supporting_line: The system matters most after someone answers.
weeks.companion_post: Explain how replies get classified, routed and followed up. Keep volume separate from qualified opportunities.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: The system matters most after someone answers.

weeks.headline: An AI demo works on the happy path.
weeks.supporting_line: A product has to handle missing fields, strange inputs and wrong answers.
weeks.companion_post: Share three failure cases you now test before trusting an AI workflow. Do not invent an incident; use real examples from your work.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: A product has to handle missing fields, strange inputs and wrong answers.

weeks.headline: If a human still copies the answer into the CRM, the workflow isn’t finished.
weeks.supporting_line: Close the loop: update the record, assign an owner, show the next step.
weeks.companion_post: Map a before/after handoff without claiming time savings you have not measured.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Close the loop: update the record, assign an owner, show the next step.

weeks.headline: I moved closer to the code because handoffs hide too much.
weeks.supporting_line: Product decisions make more sense when you see what it takes to ship them.
weeks.companion_post: Describe a real moment from your product career that changed how you work. Add a specific detail only you would know.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Product decisions make more sense when you see what it takes to ship them.

weeks.headline: Not every AI idea deserves an agent.
weeks.supporting_line: Sometimes a rule, an API call and one human check are enough.
weeks.companion_post: Give a decision test for choosing between rules, a workflow, RAG and an agent.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Sometimes a rule, an API call and one human check are enough.

weeks.headline: A voice assistant needs to know when to stop talking.
weeks.supporting_line: Escalation is part of the experience—not a failure state.
weeks.companion_post: Explain what a good human handoff should preserve: caller context, reason and transcript.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Escalation is part of the experience—not a failure state.

weeks.headline: Bring one repetitive task. Not a 40-slide AI strategy.
weeks.supporting_line: We’ll map the current steps and decide whether automation is worth it.
weeks.companion_post: Explain what happens in a ProdCraft discovery/build session and what you will not promise before scoping.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Use this CTA only if the 30-minute session and described process are currently offered.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: We’ll map the current steps and decide whether automation is worth it.

weeks.headline: A roadmap item is not a business outcome.
weeks.supporting_line: Name what should change for the user after the feature ships.
weeks.companion_post: Show how you would rewrite a vague AI roadmap item as an observable user or business change.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Name what should change for the user after the feature ships.

weeks.headline: A workflow without an owner is just a script.
weeks.supporting_line: Who acts when the model is uncertain, the API fails or the customer needs a person?
weeks.companion_post: Walk through ownership across the workflow: trigger, automation, exception, human and audit trail.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Who acts when the model is uncertain, the API fails or the customer needs a person?

weeks.headline: More sends won’t fix a weak list.
weeks.supporting_line: Data quality and deliverability set the ceiling before copy gets a chance.
weeks.companion_post: Share a pre-flight checklist: source quality, domain health, validation, audience fit and stop conditions.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Data quality and deliverability set the ceiling before copy gets a chance.

weeks.headline: RAG can retrieve the wrong truth very quickly.
weeks.supporting_line: If the source documents are stale or contradictory, retrieval won’t fix that.
weeks.companion_post: Explain document ownership, freshness, citations and what to do when sources conflict.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: If the source documents are stale or contradictory, retrieval won’t fix that.

weeks.headline: One good answer is not an evaluation set.
weeks.supporting_line: Keep real questions and past failures as regression tests.
weeks.companion_post: Show a tiny example of a test set: input, expected behaviour, failure mode and release threshold.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Keep real questions and past failures as regression tests.

weeks.headline: The boring code can protect the whole business process.
weeks.supporting_line: Deduplication prevents the same lead or invoice from being processed twice.
weeks.companion_post: Describe idempotency in plain English, with a harmless example from an automation.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Deduplication prevents the same lead or invoice from being processed twice.

weeks.headline: The work after send is where outbound gets operational.
weeks.supporting_line: In the documented baseline: about 24,000 emails a month and a 4% reply rate.
weeks.companion_post: Only publish the numbers if send logs and reply definitions are verified. Explain reply routing and lead ownership—not just volume.
weeks.publish_guardrail: VERIFY against actual send logs and exact reply-rate denominator before publishing; use 24,000/month baseline only if still accurate.
weeks.fallback_supporting_line: Reply routing, lead ownership and follow-up are where outbound becomes an operation.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Reply routing, lead ownership and follow-up are where outbound becomes an operation.

weeks.headline: A pilot isn’t a product yet.
weeks.supporting_line: Production adds permissions, support, cost controls and failure handling.
weeks.companion_post: Use a pilot-to-production checklist with one concrete example per category.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Production adds permissions, support, cost controls and failure handling.

weeks.headline: If the call gets unusual, can the assistant recover?
weeks.supporting_line: Test interruptions, unclear requests, silence and requests for a person.
weeks.companion_post: Describe a voice-agent test plan and the exact handoff conditions you would require.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Test interruptions, unclear requests, silence and requests for a person.

weeks.headline: I don’t want AI in every workflow.
weeks.supporting_line: I want fewer repetitive decisions and clearer ownership.
weeks.companion_post: Explain one kind of task you would not automate and why. Be specific about risk or low frequency.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: I want fewer repetitive decisions and clearer ownership.

weeks.headline: A reply in a shared inbox is a handoff waiting to fail.
weeks.supporting_line: Classify it, assign it and make the next action visible.
weeks.companion_post: Show a simple reply-routing taxonomy: interested, objection, referral, unsubscribe, out of office and needs review.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Classify it, assign it and make the next action visible.

weeks.headline: Your software should not depend on your consultant staying forever.
weeks.supporting_line: The repo, cloud account, credentials and runbook should be yours.
weeks.companion_post: Explain what a clean handover includes. Only promise terms that your contracts and actual process support.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Publish only if contract and actual delivery process guarantee these ownership/handover terms.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: The repo, cloud account, credentials and runbook should be yours.

weeks.headline: Start with the task, not the model.
weeks.supporting_line: What decision gets easier? What work disappears? What new risk appears?
weeks.companion_post: Apply those three questions to one real use case, without turning the post into a tool comparison.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: What decision gets easier? What work disappears? What new risk appears?

weeks.headline: A reply rate alone won’t tell you whether outbound works.
weeks.supporting_line: Track qualified conversations and next steps—not only sends and opens.
weeks.companion_post: Show the measurement chain from delivered message to reply, qualified conversation, meeting and opportunity. Clearly mark estimates.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Track qualified conversations and next steps—not only sends and opens.

weeks.headline: A confident answer with no source is a product problem.
weeks.supporting_line: Show the evidence—or say the system cannot verify it.
weeks.companion_post: Describe when source links, citations or a refusal are more useful than a fluent answer.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Show the evidence—or say the system cannot verify it.

weeks.headline: Automation should remove a step, not add another dashboard.
weeks.supporting_line: If someone must copy the result by hand, close the loop.
weeks.companion_post: Pick one workflow and mark every manual handoff that remains after the proposed automation.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: If someone must copy the result by hand, close the loop.

weeks.headline: A marketplace is more than a checkout page.
weeks.supporting_line: A partner build processed $85K in its first three months; payment edge cases mattered too.
weeks.companion_post: Use only with permission and accurate attribution to the partner agency. Explain one concrete payment or onboarding decision.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Confirm partner permission, attribution and $85K / three-month figure before publishing.
weeks.fallback_supporting_line: In a partner marketplace build, payment edge cases mattered as much as the checkout.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: In a partner marketplace build, payment edge cases mattered as much as the checkout.

weeks.headline: Every prompt change can break something that used to work.
weeks.supporting_line: Version prompts and rerun the failures you already know about.
weeks.companion_post: Explain a lightweight prompt regression process. Avoid suggesting that evaluation guarantees correctness.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Version prompts and rerun the failures you already know about.

weeks.headline: The useful part of an AI assistant is what happens after the answer.
weeks.supporting_line: Create the task, update the record or notify the right person.
weeks.companion_post: Show a simple end-to-end chain from request to action to confirmation and exception handling.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Create the task, update the record or notify the right person.

weeks.headline: A green test suite doesn’t mean the feature is useful.
weeks.supporting_line: Test the real task, with messy inputs and the people who will use it.
weeks.companion_post: Contrast a technical pass with a user outcome; propose a small acceptance test.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Test the real task, with messy inputs and the people who will use it.

weeks.headline: The latency fix wasn’t “use a bigger model.”
weeks.supporting_line: Routing, caching and evaluation can matter as much as the model choice.
weeks.companion_post: Use the Wiser-related experience only if disclosure is permitted; explain the mechanism and confirm every numeric result before adding it.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Do not publish numerical Wiser outcomes unless supported by source documents and disclosure permission.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Routing, caching and evaluation can matter as much as the model choice.

weeks.headline: Personalization should be a fact, not a guess.
weeks.supporting_line: If you can’t point to the source, don’t put it in the email.
weeks.companion_post: Show how you would distinguish verified company facts from inferred or fabricated personalization.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: If you can’t point to the source, don’t put it in the email.

weeks.headline: A failed tool call should not look like a successful answer.
weeks.supporting_line: Make failures visible, recover safely and give the human enough context.
weeks.companion_post: Describe status handling, retries, timeouts and the user-facing fallback.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Make failures visible, recover safely and give the human enough context.

weeks.headline: The stack is the easy part. Choosing what not to build is harder.
weeks.supporting_line: Scope one painful workflow before debating frameworks.
weeks.companion_post: Tell a short story about reducing scope or choosing a simpler solution. Use a real example.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Scope one painful workflow before debating frameworks.

weeks.headline: A prototype should answer one risky question.
weeks.supporting_line: Can this work with our data, our users and our constraints?
weeks.companion_post: Offer a three-question prototype brief: assumption, evidence, decision.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Can this work with our data, our users and our constraints?

weeks.headline: If an alert has no owner, it’s just another notification.
weeks.supporting_line: Every alert needs a next action, an escalation path and a runbook.
weeks.companion_post: Show a sample alert-to-resolution sequence, including what happens outside business hours.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Every alert needs a next action, an escalation path and a runbook.

weeks.headline: The cheapest model can be expensive if it needs three retries.
weeks.supporting_line: Measure cost per successful task, not just cost per token.
weeks.companion_post: Explain the trade-off between model price, retries, latency and human review. Use measured costs only.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Measure cost per successful task, not just cost per token.

weeks.headline: The fastest response is useless if it reaches the wrong person.
weeks.supporting_line: Routing and CRM hygiene are part of the product.
weeks.companion_post: Show the minimum fields and ownership rules needed to route an inbound or outbound reply.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Routing and CRM hygiene are part of the product.

weeks.headline: Human review isn’t the problem. Surprise review is.
weeks.supporting_line: Decide in advance which cases need a person.
weeks.companion_post: Define escalation triggers such as low confidence, sensitive data, high-value actions or contradictory sources.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Decide in advance which cases need a person.

weeks.headline: The first version should be small enough to learn from.
weeks.supporting_line: Keep the scope narrow; keep the acceptance criteria real.
weeks.companion_post: Explain what you would include—and explicitly exclude—from a first release for one use case.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Keep the scope narrow; keep the acceptance criteria real.

weeks.headline: The hardest automation bugs live between systems.
weeks.supporting_line: A webhook fires twice. A record changes late. A reply arrives out of order.
weeks.companion_post: Use a real or clearly labelled illustrative sequence to explain deduplication, retries and reconciliation.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: A webhook fires twice. A record changes late. A reply arrives out of order.

weeks.headline: After 15 years in product, I still start with the same question.
weeks.supporting_line: What is the user trying to get done—and what gets in the way?
weeks.companion_post: Personal reflection connecting product management to hands-on building. Avoid generic career inspiration.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: What is the user trying to get done—and what gets in the way?

weeks.headline: “Can I speak to a person?” is a core test case.
weeks.supporting_line: A good voice assistant makes the handoff easier, not awkward.
weeks.companion_post: Write the exact handoff behaviour you would test and what context must follow the caller.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: A good voice assistant makes the handoff easier, not awkward.

weeks.headline: Your document assistant needs a plan for stale documents.
weeks.supporting_line: Show dates, source ownership and what happens when two documents disagree.
weeks.companion_post: Give readers a four-point document hygiene checklist before any RAG build.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Show dates, source ownership and what happens when two documents disagree.

weeks.headline: A timeline is not a plan until the risks are visible.
weeks.supporting_line: Data access, integrations, permissions and ownership often decide the schedule.
weeks.companion_post: Share a scoping template that names assumptions, dependencies, unknowns and a first milestone.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Data access, integrations, permissions and ownership often decide the schedule.

weeks.headline: Speed is not skipping the controls.
weeks.supporting_line: It is removing unnecessary handoffs while keeping checks that catch real failures.
weeks.companion_post: Explain the minimum release safeguards you believe every automation needs. Distinguish must-haves from context-dependent choices.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: It is removing unnecessary handoffs while keeping checks that catch real failures.

weeks.headline: Outbound needs an off switch.
weeks.supporting_line: Pause safely when deliverability drops or an integration starts misbehaving.
weeks.companion_post: Explain stop conditions and monitoring in a responsible outbound system; avoid presenting volume as the goal.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Pause safely when deliverability drops or an integration starts misbehaving.

weeks.headline: A live demo beats a paragraph saying “production-ready.”
weeks.supporting_line: Try the multilingual CV optimizer with a real role and your own criteria.
weeks.companion_post: Show a short screen recording of the live tool, the input, the output and one limitation. Link to the demo in the post text.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Verify demo still works and show a real screen recording; do not overstate evaluation claims.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Try the multilingual CV optimizer with a real role and your own criteria.

weeks.headline: A good build should leave your team more capable.
weeks.supporting_line: Documentation, access and a clear runbook are part of delivery.
weeks.companion_post: Show what the handover checklist includes and what the client owns afterwards. Promise only what your engagement terms guarantee.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Publish only if contract and actual delivery process guarantee these ownership/handover terms.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Documentation, access and a clear runbook are part of delivery.

weeks.headline: Bring me the task that lives in three tabs and one person’s head.
weeks.supporting_line: We’ll map the workflow and decide whether automation is worth the complexity.
weeks.companion_post: Describe the 30-minute session: map current state, identify risks, decide whether to prototype. Avoid implying a guaranteed build plan for every case.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Use this CTA only if the 30-minute session and described process are currently offered.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: We’ll map the workflow and decide whether automation is worth the complexity.

weeks.headline: Before hiring for an AI project, define the result you’re buying.
weeks.supporting_line: A job title and a tech stack are not a business case.
weeks.companion_post: Give a short brief template: user, problem, current cost, desired change, constraints and success measure.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: A job title and a tech stack are not a business case.

weeks.headline: No AI pitch deck. One real workflow.
weeks.supporting_line: Bring a repetitive task; leave with a clearer decision on what to build—or not build.
weeks.companion_post: End the series by explaining how ProdCraft scopes a small first step and when you would advise a client not to automate.
weeks.publish_guardrail: Use this CTA only if the 30-minute session and described process are currently offered.
weeks.rendered_supporting_line: Bring a repetitive task; leave with a clearer decision on what to build—or not build.
